Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

# Workflow authoring reference

A workflow structures work across many agents — to be comprehensive (decompose and cover in parallel), to be confident (independent perspectives and adversarial checks before committing), or to take on scale one context can't hold (migrations, audits, broad sweeps). The script is where you encode that structure: what fans out, what verifies, what synthesizes.

When you do call it, the right move is often **hybrid**: scout inline first (list the files, find the channels, scope the diff) to discover the work-list, then call Workflow to pipeline over it. You don't need to know the shape before the *task* — only before the *orchestration step*.

Common single-phase workflows you can chain across turns:
- **Understand** — parallel readers over relevant subsystems → structured map
- **Design** — judge panel of N independent approaches → scored synthesis
- **Review** — dimensions → find → adversarially verify (the review-changes example)
- **Research** — multi-modal sweep → deep-read → synthesize
- **Migrate** — discover sites → transform each (worktree isolation) → verify

For larger work, run several in sequence — read each result before deciding the next phase. You stay in the loop; each workflow is one well-scoped fan-out.

**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

19		ID         string          `json:"attachmentId"`
20		TotalBytes json.RawMessage `json:"totalBytes"`
21		ChunkSize  json.RawMessage `json:"chunkSize"`

25	// attachmentListEntry is one item of the attachment listing response.
26	type attachmentListEntry struct {
27		ID             string  `json:"attachmentId"`
28		TotalBytes     int64   `json:"totalBytes"`
29		ChunkSize      int64   `json:"chunkSize"`
30		SHA256         string  `json:"sha256"`

36	// handleListAttachments is the read-only listing over the attachment
37	// collection: every upload the device in the path created plus every upload
38	// another device created and granted it read access to, each at most once,
39	// ordered by creation ascending. limit (1..1000, default 100) and offset
40	// (non-negative, default 0) page the result; an illegal value is a 400 JSON
41	// error checked before the device lookup. An unregistered device is a 404
42	// JSON error with no listing. The handler writes nothing: no attachment,
43	// chunk or access state changes.
44	func handleListAttachments(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
45		deviceID := r.PathValue("deviceId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
46	
47		limit, offset, ok := parseAttachmentListQuery(w, r)
48		if !ok {
49			return
50		}
51	
52		items, err := s.ListAttachments(deviceID, limit, offset)
53		if err != nil {
54			switch {
55			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDeviceNotFound):
56				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "device not found")
57			default:
58				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to list attachments")
59			}
60			return
61		}
62	
63		entries := make([]attachmentListEntry, 0, len(items))
64		for _, item := range items {
65			entries = append(entries, attachmentListEntry{
66				ID:             item.ID,
67				TotalBytes:     item.TotalBytes,
68				ChunkSize:      item.ChunkSize,
69				SHA256:         item.SHA256,
70				Complete:       item.Complete,
71				Owned:          item.Owned,
72				ReceivedChunks: item.ReceivedChunks,
73			})
74		}
75	
76		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"attachments": entries})
77	}

79	// parseAttachmentListQuery parses the limit/offset pagination parameters of
80	// the attachment listing, writing the documented 400 on an illegal value.
81	func parseAttachmentListQuery(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) (limit, offset int64, ok bool) {
82		q := r.URL.Query()
83	
84		limit = defaultListLimit
85		if raw := q.Get("limit"); raw != "" {
86			v, err := strconv.ParseInt(raw, 10, 64)
87			if err != nil || v < 1 || v > maxListLimit {
88				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "limit must be an integer between 1 and 1000")
89				return 0, 0, false
90			}
91			limit = v
92		}
93	
94		offset = 0
95		if raw := q.Get("offset"); raw != "" {
96			v, err := strconv.ParseInt(raw, 10, 64)
97			if err != nil || v < 0 {
98				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "offset must be a non-negative integer")
99				return 0, 0, false
100			}
101			offset = v
102		}

104		return limit, offset, true

107	// handleCreateAttachment registers a resumable chunked upload for the device
108	// in the path. The body is strict JSON carrying the stable attachment id, the
109	// declared total size and chunk size (positive integers) and the lowercase
110	// hex SHA-256 of the final content. Any malformed input is a 400 JSON error
111	// and writes nothing; an unregistered device is a 404; an id already taken —
112	// by another device, or by this device with different metadata — is a 409
113	// that leaves the original record untouched.
114	func handleCreateAttachment(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
115		deviceID := r.PathValue("deviceId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
116

118		if !decodeJSONBody(w, r, &req) {
119			return
120		}

123			return
124		}
125		totalBytes, ok := parsePositiveInt(req.TotalBytes)
126		if !ok {

128			return

131		if !ok {
132			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "chunkSize must be a positive integer")
133			return
134		}
135		if !isLowerHexSHA256(req.SHA256) {
136			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "sha256 must be 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters")
137			return

139	
140		created, err := s.CreateAttachment(deviceID, store.Attachment{
141			ID:         req.ID,
142			TotalBytes: totalBytes,
143			ChunkSize:  chunkSize,
144			SHA256:     req.SHA256,
145		})
146		if err != nil {
147			var conflict *store.ErrAttachmentConflict
148			switch {
149			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDeviceNotFound):
150				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "device not found")
151			case errors.As(err, &conflict):
152				writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "attachmentId already exists with a different owner or metadata: "+conflict.ID)
153			default:
154				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to create attachment")
155			}
156			return

159		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"attachmentId": req.ID, "created": created})

162	// handlePutChunk stores one binary chunk of an upload. The request must be
163	// application/octet-stream; the index is zero-based and chunks may arrive in
164	// any order. An unknown attachment is a 404 and a non-creator device a 403; a
165	// wrong content type, an out-of-range index, a short non-final chunk or a
166	// final chunk beyond the declared total is a 400 — none of these write
167	// anything. Re-submitting identical bytes is idempotent; different bytes for
168	// the same index are a 409 and the first content is kept. Once the upload is
169	// finished it is sealed: every further chunk write, even a byte-identical
170	// one, is a 409 and the stored content is unchanged.
171	func handlePutChunk(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
172		deviceID := r.PathValue("deviceId")         // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
173		attachmentID := r.PathValue("attachmentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
174	
175		mediaType, _, err := mime.ParseMediaType(r.Header.Get("Content-Type"))
176		if err != nil || mediaType != "application/octet-stream" {
177			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "Content-Type must be application/octet-stream")
178			return
179		}
180	
181		index, ok := parseCursorPath(r.PathValue("index"))
182		if !ok {
183			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "chunk index must be a non-negative integer")
184			return
185		}
186	
187		r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, maxChunkBytes+1)
188		data, err := io.ReadAll(r.Body)
189		if err != nil || int64(len(data)) > maxChunkBytes {
190			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "chunk body is too large")
191			return
192		}
193	
194		created, err := s.PutChunk(deviceID, attachmentID, index, data)
195		if err != nil {
196			var invalid *store.ErrChunkInvalid
197			var conflict *store.ErrChunkConflict
198			switch {
199			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentNotFound):
200				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "attachment not found")
201			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentForbidden):
202				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "attachment belongs to another device")
203			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentSealed):
204				writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "attachment is complete and no longer accepts chunks")
205			case errors.As(err, &invalid):
206				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, invalid.Reason)
207			case errors.As(err, &conflict):
208				writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "chunk already exists with different content")
209			default:
210				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to store chunk")
211			}
212			return
213		}
214	
215		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"index": index, "created": created})
216	}

218	// handleCompleteAttachment seals an upload. Only the creating device may
219	// finish it (others get a 403; an unknown attachment a 404). Missing chunks
220	// or a total-length mismatch are a 409 and leave the upload resumable; a
221	// digest mismatch is a 422 and leaves it incomplete. When another finished
222	// attachment already holds the same digest and size, the content is reused
223	// without copying bytes (reused=true); the same digest at a different size is
224	// a 409. A successful or repeated finish returns the same recorded result.
225	func handleCompleteAttachment(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
226		deviceID := r.PathValue("deviceId")         // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
227		attachmentID := r.PathValue("attachmentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
228	
229		result, err := s.CompleteAttachment(deviceID, attachmentID)
230		if err != nil {
231			switch {
232			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentNotFound):
233				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "attachment not found")
234			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentForbidden):
235				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "attachment belongs to another device")
236			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentIncomplete):
237				writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "chunks are missing or do not add up to the declared total")
238			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentDigestMismatch):
239				writeError(w, http.StatusUnprocessableEntity, "assembled content does not match the declared sha256")
240			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentDigestConflict):
241				writeError(w, http.StatusConflict, "a completed content with the same digest but a different size exists")
242			default:
243				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to complete attachment")
244			}
245			return
246		}
247	
248		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, result)
249	}

252	// metadata, the sorted indices received so far and the completion status. The
253	// creator and any device granted access through the access endpoint see the
254	// same body; any other device gets a 403, an unknown attachment a 404.
255	func handleGetAttachment(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
256		deviceID := r.PathValue("deviceId")         // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
257		attachmentID := r.PathValue("attachmentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
258

273			"attachmentId":   a.ID,
274			"totalBytes":     a.TotalBytes,

276			"sha256":         a.SHA256,

284	// is a 400; an unknown attachment or a chunk that never arrived is a 404; any
285	// other device is a 403.
286	func handleGetChunk(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
287		deviceID := r.PathValue("deviceId")         // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
288		attachmentID := r.PathValue("attachmentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty

291		if !ok {
292			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "chunk index must be a non-negative integer")
293			return
294		}

296		data, err := s.GetAttachmentChunk(deviceID, attachmentID, index)
297		if err != nil {
298			var invalid *store.ErrChunkInvalid
299			switch {
300			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentNotFound):
301				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "attachment not found")
302			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrChunkNotFound):
303				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "chunk not found")

319	// handleSetAttachmentAccess grants or revokes a registered device's read
320	// access to one attachment. Every (attachment, device) pair starts
321	// unauthorized, so the first grant is the first write; repeating the current
322	// state is idempotent (changed=false). Only the creator may change access: a
323	// non-creator caller gets a 403 and an unknown attachment a 404, neither
324	// touching any access state. A rejected request (bad content type, malformed
325	// JSON, trailing content, empty or mistyped fields, unknown action) is a 400
326	// JSON error and writes nothing; an unregistered target device is a 404 JSON
327	// error. A granted device reads the same metadata and chunk bytes as the
328	// creator; a revoke returns its reads to 403 at once and never deletes
329	// stored chunks or sealed content.
330	func handleSetAttachmentAccess(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
331		deviceID := r.PathValue("deviceId")         // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
332		attachmentID := r.PathValue("attachmentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
333	
334		var req permissionRequest
335		if !decodeJSONBody(w, r, &req) {
336			return
337		}
338		if req.DeviceID == "" {
339			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "deviceId must be a non-empty string")
340			return
341		}
342		var authorized bool
343		switch req.Action {
344		case "grant":
345			authorized = true
346		case "revoke":
347			authorized = false
348		default:
349			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, `action must be "grant" or "revoke"`)
350			return
351		}
352	
353		changed, err := s.SetAttachmentAccess(deviceID, attachmentID, req.DeviceID, authorized)
354		if err != nil {
355			switch {
356			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentNotFound):
357				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "attachment not found")
358			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentForbidden):
359				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "attachment belongs to another device")
360			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrDeviceNotFound):
361				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "device not found")
362			default:
363				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to update attachment access")
364			}
365			return
366		}
367	
368		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{
369			"deviceId":   req.DeviceID,
370			"authorized": authorized,
371			"changed":    changed,
372		})
373	}

375	// handleDeleteAttachment removes an upload outright. Only the creating device
376	// may delete: any other device gets a 403 and an unknown (or already deleted)
377	// id a 404, neither writing anything. A successful delete answers the
378	// attachment id and a deletion marker, after which the record, its chunks,
379	// its completion state and every access grant are gone: every later read,
380	// chunk write, finish or access change against the id is a 404, and
381	// re-creating the id starts a brand-new upload. Digest-addressed content is
382	// reclaimed only when no finished attachment references it any longer.
383	func handleDeleteAttachment(s *app.App, w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
384		deviceID := r.PathValue("deviceId")         // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
385		attachmentID := r.PathValue("attachmentId") // route pattern + guard guarantee non-empty
386	
387		if err := s.DeleteAttachment(deviceID, attachmentID); err != nil {
388			switch {
389			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentNotFound):
390				writeError(w, http.StatusNotFound, "attachment not found")
391			case errors.Is(err, store.ErrAttachmentForbidden):
392				writeError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "attachment belongs to another device")
393			default:
394				writeError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, "failed to delete attachment")
395			}
396			return
397		}
398	
399		writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"attachmentId": attachmentID, "deleted": true})
400	}

402	// isLowerHexSHA256 reports whether s is exactly 64 lowercase hex characters.
403	func isLowerHexSHA256(s string) bool {
404		if len(s) != 64 {
405			return false
406		}
407		for _, c := range s {
408			if (c < '0' || c > '9') && (c < 'a' || c > 'f') {
409				return false
410			}
411		}
412		return true
413	}

75	// Attachment is the stored metadata of one resumable upload.
76	type Attachment struct {
77		ID         string

95	// chunkCount returns how many chunks the declared shape implies.
96	func (a Attachment) chunkCount() int64 {
97		return (a.TotalBytes + a.ChunkSize - 1) / a.ChunkSize
98	}
99	
100	// checkChunkShape validates index and len(data) against the declared
101	// totalBytes/chunkSize, returning *ErrChunkInvalid on any violation.
102	func (a Attachment) checkChunkShape(index int64, length int64) error {
103		count := a.chunkCount()
104		if index < 0 || index >= count {
105			return &ErrChunkInvalid{Reason: fmt.Sprintf("chunk index %d is out of range [0, %d)", index, count)}
106		}
107		if index < count-1 {
108			if length != a.ChunkSize {
109				return &ErrChunkInvalid{Reason: fmt.Sprintf("non-final chunk %d must be exactly %d bytes", index, a.ChunkSize)}
110			}
111			return nil
112		}
113		remaining := a.TotalBytes - a.ChunkSize*(count-1)
114		if length < 1 || length > remaining {
115			return &ErrChunkInvalid{Reason: fmt.Sprintf("final chunk must be between 1 and %d bytes", remaining)}
116		}
117		return nil
118	}

120	// loadAttachmentTx loads an attachment row inside tx without any ownership
121	// judgment; an unknown id yields ErrAttachmentNotFound.
122	func loadAttachmentTx(tx *sql.Tx, id string) (Attachment, error) {
123		var a Attachment
124		var complete, reused int
125		err := tx.QueryRow(
126			`SELECT id, device_id, total_bytes, chunk_size, sha256, complete, reused
127			 FROM attachments WHERE id = ?`, id,
128		).Scan(&a.ID, &a.DeviceID, &a.TotalBytes, &a.ChunkSize, &a.SHA256, &complete, &reused)
129		switch {
130		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
131			return Attachment{}, ErrAttachmentNotFound
132		case err != nil:
133			return Attachment{}, err
134		}
135		a.Complete = complete != 0
136		a.Reused = reused != 0
137		return a, nil
138	}

155	// access: the creator, or a device the creator has granted access through
156	// SetAttachmentAccess, may read; any other device yields
157	// ErrAttachmentForbidden. An unknown id yields ErrAttachmentNotFound.
158	func getAttachmentReadTx(tx *sql.Tx, id, deviceID string) (Attachment, error) {
159		a, err := loadAttachmentTx(tx, id)
160		if err != nil {
161			return Attachment{}, err

164			return a, nil
165		}

172		}

176	// attachmentAccessGrantedTx reports whether deviceID currently holds read
177	// access to the attachment. Every (attachment, device) pair starts
178	// unauthorized, so an absent row means not granted.
179	func attachmentAccessGrantedTx(tx *sql.Tx, attachmentID, deviceID string) (bool, error) {
180		var stored int
181		err := tx.QueryRow(
182			`SELECT authorized FROM attachment_access WHERE attachment_id = ? AND device_id = ?`,
183			attachmentID, deviceID,
184		).Scan(&stored)
185		switch {
186		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
187			return false, nil
188		case err != nil:
189			return false, err
190		default:
191			return stored != 0, nil
192		}

195	// CreateAttachment registers a new resumable upload owned by deviceID.
196	//
197	//   - An unregistered device yields ErrDeviceNotFound; nothing is written.
198	//   - Re-posting identical metadata under the same device is idempotent
199	//     (created=false).
200	//   - An id already taken — by another device (even with identical metadata)
201	//     or by this device with different metadata — yields
202	//     *ErrAttachmentConflict; the original record is unchanged.
203	//
204	// The check and the insert run in one serialized transaction and commit
205	// synchronously, so a retry after a crash reaches the same decision.
206	func (s *Store) CreateAttachment(deviceID string, a Attachment) (created bool, err error) {
207		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
208		if err != nil {
209			return false, err
210		}
211		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
212	
213		var deviceExists bool
214		if err := tx.QueryRow(
215			`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM devices WHERE id = ?)`, deviceID,
216		).Scan(&deviceExists); err != nil {
217			return false, err
218		}
219		if !deviceExists {
220			return false, ErrDeviceNotFound
221		}
222	
223		var owner string
224		var totalBytes, chunkSize int64
225		var digest string
226		err = tx.QueryRow(
227			`SELECT device_id, total_bytes, chunk_size, sha256 FROM attachments WHERE id = ?`, a.ID,
228		).Scan(&owner, &totalBytes, &chunkSize, &digest)
229		switch {
230		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
231			// The creation sequence is one past the current maximum, assigned
232			// inside the same serialized transaction as the insert, so values are
233			// unique, monotone and never reused — a deleted id that is created
234			// again lists as a brand-new record at the end.
235			if _, err := tx.Exec(
236				`INSERT INTO attachments (id, device_id, total_bytes, chunk_size, sha256, complete, reused, created_seq)
237				 VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 0, 0, (SELECT COALESCE(MAX(created_seq), 0) + 1 FROM attachments))`,
238				a.ID, deviceID, a.TotalBytes, a.ChunkSize, a.SHA256,
239			); err != nil {
240				return false, err
241			}
242			if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
243				return false, err
244			}
245			return true, nil
246		case err != nil:
247			return false, err
248		}
249	
250		if owner != deviceID || totalBytes != a.TotalBytes || chunkSize != a.ChunkSize || digest != a.SHA256 {
251			return false, &ErrAttachmentConflict{ID: a.ID}
252		}
253		return false, tx.Commit()
254	}

256	// PutChunk stores one chunk of an upload, durably, inside one transaction.
257	//
258	// Ownership and shape are enforced first: an unknown attachment yields
259	// ErrAttachmentNotFound, a non-creator device ErrAttachmentForbidden, and an
260	// out-of-range index or wrong length *ErrChunkInvalid — none of these write
261	// anything. A finished upload is sealed: any further chunk write, even a
262	// byte-identical resubmission, yields ErrAttachmentSealed and changes
263	// nothing. On an open upload, re-submitting identical bytes for an existing
264	// index is idempotent (created=false); different bytes for the same index
265	// yield *ErrChunkConflict and the first content is kept. Chunks may arrive in
266	// any order.
267	func (s *Store) PutChunk(deviceID, attachmentID string, index int64, data []byte) (created bool, err error) {
268		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
269		if err != nil {
270			return false, err
271		}
272		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
273	
274		a, err := getAttachmentTx(tx, attachmentID, deviceID)
275		if err != nil {
276			return false, err
277		}
278		// A sealed upload is immutable: reject every further write before any
279		// shape check or content comparison, so the recorded state and content
280		// cannot change once the finish committed.
281		if a.Complete {
282			return false, ErrAttachmentSealed
283		}
284		if err := a.checkChunkShape(index, int64(len(data))); err != nil {
285			return false, err
286		}
287	
288		var existing []byte
289		err = tx.QueryRow(
290			`SELECT data FROM attachment_chunks WHERE attachment_id = ? AND idx = ?`,
291			attachmentID, index,
292		).Scan(&existing)
293		switch {
294		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
295			if _, err := tx.Exec(
296				`INSERT INTO attachment_chunks (attachment_id, idx, data) VALUES (?, ?, ?)`,
297				attachmentID, index, data,
298			); err != nil {
299				return false, err
300			}
301			if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
302				return false, err
303			}
304			return true, nil
305		case err != nil:
306			return false, err
307		}
308	
309		if !bytesEqual(existing, data) {
310			return false, &ErrChunkConflict{Index: index}
311		}
312		return false, tx.Commit()
313	}

315	// reuseContentTx resolves the digest-addressed content reuse decision inside
316	// tx: it returns reused=true when finished content with the same digest and
317	// size already exists (the bytes are not copied), reused=false when no such
318	// content exists yet (the caller inserts it), and ErrAttachmentDigestConflict
319	// when a finished content carries the same digest but a different size. That
320	// last state cannot arise from honest chunk assembly without a hash collision,
321	// but it must never silently reuse mismatched bytes.
322	func reuseContentTx(tx *sql.Tx, digest string, size int64) (bool, error) {
323		var contentSize int64
324		err := tx.QueryRow(
325			`SELECT size FROM attachment_contents WHERE sha256 = ?`, digest,
326		).Scan(&contentSize)
327		switch {
328		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
329			return false, nil
330		case err != nil:
331			return false, err
332		case contentSize != size:
333			return false, ErrAttachmentDigestConflict
334		default:
335			return true, nil
336		}
337	}

339	// CompleteAttachment seals an upload: every declared chunk must be present
340	// and their lengths must add up to the declared total, after which the
341	// concatenated content must hash to the declared digest.
342	//
343	//   - Unknown attachment: ErrAttachmentNotFound; non-creator device:
344	//     ErrAttachmentForbidden.
345	//   - Missing chunks or a total-length mismatch: ErrAttachmentIncomplete; the
346	//     upload stays resumable.
347	//   - Digest mismatch: ErrAttachmentDigestMismatch; the upload stays
348	//     incomplete.
349	//   - A completed content with the same digest but a different size:
350	//     ErrAttachmentDigestConflict; the upload stays resumable.
351	//   - A completed content with the same digest and size is reused: the bytes
352	//     are not copied and the result carries Reused=true.
353	//
354	// A successful finish is persisted with its result, so repeating the call
355	// returns the same result without recomputing anything.
356	func (s *Store) CompleteAttachment(deviceID, attachmentID string) (CompleteResult, error) {
357		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
358		if err != nil {
359			return CompleteResult{}, err
360		}
361		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
362	
363		a, err := getAttachmentTx(tx, attachmentID, deviceID)
364		if err != nil {
365			return CompleteResult{}, err
366		}
367		if a.Complete {
368			// A repeat finish returns the recorded result unchanged.
369			return CompleteResult{
370				ID:       a.ID,
371				Size:     a.TotalBytes,
372				SHA256:   a.SHA256,
373				Complete: true,
374				Reused:   a.Reused,
375			}, tx.Commit()
376		}
377	
378		rows, err := tx.Query(
379			`SELECT idx, data FROM attachment_chunks WHERE attachment_id = ? ORDER BY idx ASC`,
380			attachmentID,
381		)
382		if err != nil {
383			return CompleteResult{}, err
384		}
385		var content []byte
386		var received int64
387		var total int64
388		var prevIndex int64 = -1
389		complete := true
390		for rows.Next() {
391			var idx int64
392			var data []byte
393			if err := rows.Scan(&idx, &data); err != nil {
394				_ = rows.Close()
395				return CompleteResult{}, err
396			}
397			if idx != prevIndex+1 {
398				complete = false
399			}
400			prevIndex = idx
401			received++
402			total += int64(len(data))
403			content = append(content, data...)
404		}
405		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
406			_ = rows.Close()
407			return CompleteResult{}, err
408		}
409		_ = rows.Close()
410	
411		if !complete || received != a.chunkCount() || total != a.TotalBytes {
412			return CompleteResult{}, ErrAttachmentIncomplete
413		}
414	
415		sum := sha256.Sum256(content)
416		if hex.EncodeToString(sum[:]) != a.SHA256 {
417			return CompleteResult{}, ErrAttachmentDigestMismatch
418		}
419	
420		// Content is addressed by digest: an existing row means another finished
421		// attachment already stored these bytes.
422		reused, err := reuseContentTx(tx, a.SHA256, a.TotalBytes)
423		if err != nil {
424			return CompleteResult{}, err
425		}
426		if !reused {
427			if _, err := tx.Exec(
428				`INSERT INTO attachment_contents (sha256, size, data) VALUES (?, ?, ?)`,
429				a.SHA256, a.TotalBytes, content,
430			); err != nil {
431				return CompleteResult{}, err
432			}
433		}
434	
435		if _, err := tx.Exec(
436			`UPDATE attachments SET complete = 1, reused = ? WHERE id = ?`,
437			boolToInt(reused), attachmentID,
438		); err != nil {
439			return CompleteResult{}, err
440		}
441		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
442			return CompleteResult{}, err
443		}
444		return CompleteResult{
445			ID:       a.ID,
446			Size:     a.TotalBytes,
447			SHA256:   a.SHA256,
448			Complete: true,
449			Reused:   reused,
450		}, nil
451	}
452	
453	// GetAttachment returns the stored metadata of an upload together with the
454	// sorted indices of the chunks received so far. An unknown id yields
455	// ErrAttachmentNotFound; a device that is neither the creator nor a granted
456	// reader yields ErrAttachmentForbidden.
457	func (s *Store) GetAttachment(deviceID, attachmentID string) (Attachment, []int64, error) {
458		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
459		if err != nil {
460			return Attachment{}, nil, err
461		}
462		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
463	
464		a, err := getAttachmentReadTx(tx, attachmentID, deviceID)
465		if err != nil {
466			return Attachment{}, nil, err
467		}
468	
469		rows, err := tx.Query(
470			`SELECT idx FROM attachment_chunks WHERE attachment_id = ? ORDER BY idx ASC`,
471			attachmentID,
472		)
473		if err != nil {
474			return Attachment{}, nil, err
475		}
476		indices := make([]int64, 0)
477		for rows.Next() {
478			var idx int64
479			if err := rows.Scan(&idx); err != nil {
480				_ = rows.Close()
481				return Attachment{}, nil, err
482			}
483			indices = append(indices, idx)
484		}
485		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
486			_ = rows.Close()
487			return Attachment{}, nil, err
488		}
489		_ = rows.Close()
490	
491		return a, indices, tx.Commit()
492	}
493	
494	// GetAttachmentChunk returns the bytes stored at index. An unknown attachment
495	// yields ErrAttachmentNotFound and a device that is neither the creator nor a
496	// granted reader yields ErrAttachmentForbidden.
497	// For a known attachment, a negative index or one beyond the declared chunk
498	// range yields *ErrChunkInvalid (the caller maps it to 400); an in-range index
499	// with no stored chunk yields ErrChunkNotFound (404).
500	func (s *Store) GetAttachmentChunk(deviceID, attachmentID string, index int64) ([]byte, error) {
501		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
502		if err != nil {
503			return nil, err
504		}
505		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
506	
507		a, err := getAttachmentReadTx(tx, attachmentID, deviceID)
508		if err != nil {
509			return nil, err
510		}
511		// The path index is already a non-negative decimal; reject one outside the
512		// shape the creator declared so out-of-range reads fail as a 400 rather than
513		// masquerading as a missing chunk (404).
514		if index < 0 || index >= a.chunkCount() {
515			return nil, &ErrChunkInvalid{Reason: fmt.Sprintf("chunk index %d is out of range [0, %d)", index, a.chunkCount())}
516		}
517	
518		var data []byte
519		err = tx.QueryRow(
520			`SELECT data FROM attachment_chunks WHERE attachment_id = ? AND idx = ?`,
521			attachmentID, index,
522		).Scan(&data)
523		switch {
524		case errors.Is(err, sql.ErrNoRows):
525			return nil, ErrChunkNotFound
526		case err != nil:
527			return nil, err
528		}
529		return data, tx.Commit()
530	}
531	
532	// DeleteAttachment removes the attachment owned by deviceID together with
533	// every trace it left behind: the received chunks, the completion state and
534	// every access grant. An unknown id yields ErrAttachmentNotFound and a device
535	// other than the creator yields ErrAttachmentForbidden — neither writes
536	// anything, so a repeat delete misses the same way a never-created id does.
537	//
538	// Finished content is addressed by digest and shared across attachments, so
539	// the stored bytes are reclaimed only when the deleted attachment was the
540	// last completed one referencing them; other finished attachments with the
541	// same digest keep reading their content unchanged. An incomplete upload
542	// references no shared content, so deleting it only drops its chunks.
543	//
544	// The check, the row removals and the content reclamation run in one
545	// serialized transaction that commits synchronously, so concurrent deletes of
546	// the same attachment commit at most once and a restart still finds the
547	// attachment gone.
548	func (s *Store) DeleteAttachment(deviceID, attachmentID string) error {
549		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
550		if err != nil {
551			return err
552		}
553		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
554	
555		a, err := getAttachmentTx(tx, attachmentID, deviceID)
556		if err != nil {
557			return err
558		}
559	
560		if _, err := tx.Exec(
561			`DELETE FROM attachment_access WHERE attachment_id = ?`, attachmentID,
562		); err != nil {
563			return err
564		}
565		if _, err := tx.Exec(
566			`DELETE FROM attachment_chunks WHERE attachment_id = ?`, attachmentID,
567		); err != nil {
568			return err
569		}
570		if _, err := tx.Exec(
571			`DELETE FROM attachments WHERE id = ?`, attachmentID,
572		); err != nil {
573			return err
574		}
575	
576		// Reclaim the digest-addressed content only when no completed attachment
577		// references it any longer.
578		if a.Complete {
579			var stillReferenced bool
580			if err := tx.QueryRow(
581				`SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM attachments WHERE sha256 = ? AND complete = 1)`,
582				a.SHA256,
583			).Scan(&stillReferenced); err != nil {
584				return err
585			}
586			if !stillReferenced {
587				if _, err := tx.Exec(
588					`DELETE FROM attachment_contents WHERE sha256 = ?`, a.SHA256,
589				); err != nil {
590					return err
591				}
592			}
593		}
594		return tx.Commit()
595	}
596	
597	// SetAttachmentAccess grants or revokes targetDeviceID's read access to the
598	// attachment, on behalf of callerDeviceID. Every (attachment, device) pair
599	// starts unauthorized, so the first grant is the first write for the pair
600	// (changed=true); repeating the state that already holds writes nothing and
601	// reports changed=false. An unknown attachment yields ErrAttachmentNotFound,
602	// a caller other than the creator ErrAttachmentForbidden, and an unregistered
603	// target device ErrDeviceNotFound — none of these write anything. The lookup
604	// and the write run in one serialized transaction, so concurrent grant/revoke
605	// calls each commit completely and the final state matches the last committed
606	// action. Access only widens the read paths; chunk writes and the finish stay
607	// creator-only, and a revoke never deletes stored chunks or sealed content.
608	func (s *Store) SetAttachmentAccess(callerDeviceID, attachmentID, targetDeviceID string, authorized bool) (changed bool, err error) {
609		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
610		if err != nil {
611			return false, err
612		}
613		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
614	
615		a, err := loadAttachmentTx(tx, attachmentID)
616		if err != nil {
617			return false, err
618		}
619		if a.DeviceID != callerDeviceID {
620			return false, ErrAttachmentForbidden
621		}
622		exists, err := DeviceExistsTx(tx, targetDeviceID)
623		if err != nil {
624			return false, err
625		}
626		if !exists {
627			return false, ErrDeviceNotFound
628		}
629	
630		current, err := attachmentAccessGrantedTx(tx, attachmentID, targetDeviceID)
631		if err != nil {
632			return false, err
633		}
634		if current == authorized {
635			return false, tx.Commit()
636		}
637	
638		v := 0
639		if authorized {
640			v = 1
641		}
642		if _, err := tx.Exec(
643			`INSERT INTO attachment_access (attachment_id, device_id, authorized) VALUES (?, ?, ?)
644			 ON CONFLICT (attachment_id, device_id) DO UPDATE SET authorized = excluded.authorized`,
645			attachmentID, targetDeviceID, v,
646		); err != nil {
647			return false, err
648		}
649		if err := tx.Commit(); err != nil {
650			return false, err
651		}
652		return true, nil
653	}
654	
655	// ListedAttachment is one entry of a device's attachment listing: the stored
656	// metadata, whether the listing device created the attachment, and the sorted
657	// indices of the chunks received so far.
658	type ListedAttachment struct {
659		Attachment
660		Owned          bool
661		ReceivedChunks []int64
662	}
663	
664	// ListAttachments returns the page of attachments visible to deviceID: every
665	// attachment the device created plus every attachment another device created
666	// and granted it read access to, each appearing at most once. Entries are
667	// ordered by creation sequence ascending — a stable order that survives
668	// restarts and never reuses a position, so a deleted id that is created again
669	// lists as a new record at the end — and paginated by limit/offset. An
670	// unregistered device yields ErrDeviceNotFound and no listing. The read runs
671	// in one serialized transaction and writes nothing.
672	func (s *Store) ListAttachments(deviceID string, limit, offset int64) ([]ListedAttachment, error) {
673		tx, err := s.db.Begin()
674		if err != nil {
675			return nil, err
676		}
677		defer func() { _ = tx.Rollback() }()
678	
679		exists, err := DeviceExistsTx(tx, deviceID)
680		if err != nil {
681			return nil, err
682		}
683		if !exists {
684			return nil, ErrDeviceNotFound
685		}
686	
687		rows, err := tx.Query(
688			`SELECT a.id, a.device_id, a.total_bytes, a.chunk_size, a.sha256, a.complete
689			 FROM attachments a
690			 WHERE a.device_id = ?
691				OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM attachment_access ac
692					WHERE ac.attachment_id = a.id AND ac.device_id = ? AND ac.authorized <> 0)
693			 ORDER BY a.created_seq ASC
694			 LIMIT ? OFFSET ?`,
695			deviceID, deviceID, limit, offset,
696		)
697		if err != nil {
698			return nil, err
699		}
700		items := make([]ListedAttachment, 0)
701		for rows.Next() {
702			var item ListedAttachment
703			var complete int
704			if err := rows.Scan(
705				&item.ID, &item.DeviceID, &item.TotalBytes, &item.ChunkSize, &item.SHA256, &complete,
706			); err != nil {
707				_ = rows.Close()
708				return nil, err
709			}
710			item.Complete = complete != 0
711			item.ReceivedChunks = make([]int64, 0)
712			items = append(items, item)
713		}
714		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
715			_ = rows.Close()
716			return nil, err
717		}
718		_ = rows.Close()
719	
720		for i := range items {
721			items[i].Owned = items[i].DeviceID == deviceID
722			chunkRows, err := tx.Query(
723				`SELECT idx FROM attachment_chunks WHERE attachment_id = ? ORDER BY idx ASC`,
724				items[i].ID,
725			)
726			if err != nil {
727				return nil, err
728			}
729			for chunkRows.Next() {
730				var idx int64
731				if err := chunkRows.Scan(&idx); err != nil {
732					_ = chunkRows.Close()
733					return nil, err
734				}
735				items[i].ReceivedChunks = append(items[i].ReceivedChunks, idx)
736			}
737			if err := chunkRows.Err(); err != nil {
738				_ = chunkRows.Close()
739				return nil, err
740			}
741			_ = chunkRows.Close()
742		}
743	
744		return items, tx.Commit()
745	}
746	
747	func bytesEqual(a, b []byte) bool {
748		if len(a) != len(b) {
749			return false
750		}
751		for i := range a {
752			if a[i] != b[i] {
753				return false
754			}
755		}
756		return true
757	}
758	
759	func boolToInt(b bool) int {
760		if b {
761			return 1
762		}
763		return 0
764	}

1	// Package app is the composition root: it opens the one shared database and
2	// constructs the three independently reusable internal services — the change
3	// event service, the permission service and the CRDT state service — wiring
4	// them together only through their internal interfaces.
5	//
6	// The services share one SQLite connection (the kernel opens a single
7	// pooled connection with immediate transactions), so a change commit, a CRDT
8	// submission or compaction, and a permission change are serialized on the
9	// same connection and leave no half-written batch. The change event and CRDT
10	// services take their registration-and-authorization verdict from the
11	// permission service inside their own transactions (events.Gate / crdt.Gate),
12	// and the permission service fans a committed revoke out to their
13	// subscription registries through authz.RevokeSink. No service reaches into
14	// another service's tables or fields.
15	//
16	// App is the single object the entry and HTTP layers use. It promotes each
17	// service's input/output boundary as its methods while hiding the wiring; it
18	// adds no authentication and exposes no endpoint of its own.
19	package app
20	
21	import (
22		"context"
23		"encoding/json"
24		"time"
25	
26		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/authz"
27		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/crdt"
28		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/events"
29		"github.com/alicegogogogogo/local-first-sync-service/internal/store"
30	)
31	
32	// App composes the durable kernel and the three internal services over one
33	// shared database connection.
34	type App struct {
35		*store.Store
36	
37		events *events.Service
38		crdt   *crdt.Service
39	
40		// Authz is the permission service. It is exposed so the HTTP layer can
41		// grant/revoke and read authorization directly; the other services reach
42		// it through their gates rather than this field.
43		Authz *authz.Service
44	}
45	
46	// Open opens (creating if needed) the SQLite database at path and constructs
47	// every internal service over it. The empty path opens a private in-memory
48	// database useful for tests. A construction failure closes the kernel and
49	// leaves nothing behind.
50	func Open(path string) (*App, error) {
51		kernel, err := store.Open(path)
52		if err != nil {
53			return nil, err
54		}
55	
56		// The permission service is built first: its gate is a constructor
57		// dependency of the change event and CRDT services.
58		permissions, err := authz.New(kernel)
59		if err != nil {
60			_ = kernel.Close()
61			return nil, err
62		}
63		eventService, err := events.New(kernel, permissions)
64		if err != nil {
65			_ = kernel.Close()
66			return nil, err
67		}
68		crdtService, err := crdt.New(kernel, permissions)
69		if err != nil {
70			_ = kernel.Close()
71			return nil, err
72		}
73	
74		// A committed revoke ends the affected live subscriptions in both
75		// push channels. The dependency is an interface, registered once here, so
76		// the permission service never names either subscriber concretely.
77		permissions.AddRevokeSink(eventsRevokeSink{eventService})
78		permissions.AddRevokeSink(crdtService)
79	
80		return &App{
81			Store:  kernel,
82			events: eventService,
83			crdt:   crdtService,
84			Authz:  permissions,
85		}, nil
86	}
87	
88	// eventsRevokeSink adapts the change event service's revoke hook to the
89	// permission service's RevokeSink interface.
90	type eventsRevokeSink struct{ e *events.Service }
91	
92	func (s eventsRevokeSink) PermissionRevoked(documentID, deviceID string) {
93		s.e.SignalRevoked(documentID, deviceID)
94	}
95	
96	// Events returns the change event service.
97	func (a *App) Events() *events.Service { return a.events }
98	
99	// CRDT returns the CRDT state service.
100	func (a *App) CRDT() *crdt.Service { return a.crdt }
101	
102	// ---- Change event service boundary (promoted so the entry layer has one
103	// object; each method delegates verbatim to the events service). ----
104	
105	// InterruptWaits wakes every parked long poll and every live change-log and
106	// CRDT subscription without closing the database, so an orderly shutdown
107	// drains waiting connections (long polls answer 503; subscriptions finish
108	// with the going-away close) instead of holding the drain hostage.
109	func (a *App) InterruptWaits() {
110		a.events.InterruptWaits()
111		a.crdt.InterruptWaits()
112	}
113	
114	// Closing reports whether shutdown has begun, covering both push channels.
115	func (a *App) Closing() bool {
116		return a.events.Closing() || a.crdt.Closing()
117	}
118	
119	// Close interrupts the in-memory observers, waits for every subscription
120	// handler to unregister and then releases the shared database handle.
121	func (a *App) Close() error {
122		a.events.InterruptWaits()
123		a.crdt.InterruptWaits()
124		a.events.WaitDrained()
125		a.crdt.WaitDrained()
126		return a.Store.Close()
127	}
128	
129	// PostChanges delegates to the change event service.
130	func (a *App) PostChanges(documentID string, changes []events.Change) ([]events.Result, error) {
131		return a.events.PostChanges(documentID, changes)
132	}
133	
134	// ReplayChanges delegates to the change event service.
135	func (a *App) ReplayChanges(documentID string, changes []events.Change) ([]events.Result, error) {
136		return a.events.ReplayChanges(documentID, changes)
137	}
138	
139	// MergeChange delegates to the change event service.
140	func (a *App) MergeChange(documentID string, baseCursor int64, c events.Change) (events.MergeResult, error) {
141		return a.events.MergeChange(documentID, baseCursor, c)
142	}
143	
144	// PutSnapshot delegates to the change event service.
145	func (a *App) PutSnapshot(documentID string, cursor int64, state json.RawMessage) (bool, error) {
146		return a.events.PutSnapshot(documentID, cursor, state)
147	}
148	
149	// GetSnapshot delegates to the change event service.
150	func (a *App) GetSnapshot(documentID string, cursor int64) (json.RawMessage, error) {
151		return a.events.GetSnapshot(documentID, cursor)
152	}
153	
154	// ExportSnapshots delegates to the change event service. A nil to means the
155	// interval has no upper bound.
156	func (a *App) ExportSnapshots(documentID string, from int64, to *int64) ([]events.ExportedSnapshot, error) {
157		return a.events.ExportSnapshots(documentID, from, to)
158	}
159	
160	// RestoreSnapshot delegates to the change event service.
161	func (a *App) RestoreSnapshot(documentID, deviceID, changeID string, snapshotCursor int64) (events.RestoreResult, error) {
162		return a.events.RestoreSnapshot(documentID, deviceID, changeID, snapshotCursor)
163	}
164	
165	// ListChanges delegates to the change event service.
166	func (a *App) ListChanges(documentID string, after, limit int64) ([]events.ListedChange, int64, error) {
167		return a.events.ListChanges(documentID, after, limit)
168	}
169	
170	// WaitForChanges delegates to the change event service.
171	func (a *App) WaitForChanges(ctx context.Context, documentID string, after, limit int64, wait time.Duration) ([]events.ListedChange, int64, bool, error) {
172		return a.events.WaitForChanges(ctx, documentID, after, limit, wait)
173	}
174	
175	// DocumentExists delegates to the change event service.
176	func (a *App) DocumentExists(documentID string) (bool, error) {
177		return a.events.DocumentExists(documentID)
178	}
179	
180	// AddSubscription delegates to the change event service.
181	func (a *App) AddSubscription(documentID, deviceID string) (<-chan struct{}, <-chan struct{}, func()) {
182		return a.events.AddSubscription(documentID, deviceID)
183	}
184	
185	// ---- Permission service boundary. ----

82	// NewHandlerWithReadiness builds the same public HTTP surface as NewHandler but
83	// answers every request — including GET /healthz — with a 503 JSON error until
84	// ready reports that the database is open and the listener is accepting
85	// connections. Once ready, responses are byte-for-byte what NewHandler emits;
86	// readiness is one-way, so a later flip back is not part of the contract.
87	func NewHandlerWithReadiness(s *app.App, ready func() bool) http.Handler {
88		h := NewHandler(s)

93			if !ready() {
94				writeError(w, http.StatusServiceUnavailable, "service is not ready")
95				return
96			}
97			h.ServeHTTP(w, r)
98		})

299	// emptyIDGuard rejects requests carrying an empty path identifier with a 400
300	// JSON error instead of letting ServeMux emit its HTML redirect or a
301	// plain-text 404.
302	//
303	// The document family keeps its original rule (an empty documentID, i.e. the
304	// prefix /v1/documents//); other odd paths there retain their old response so
305	// the pre-existing surface is unchanged. The new device/session families are
306	// stricter: any doubled slash (an empty deviceId, sessionId or documentId
307	// segment) or a trailing slash (an empty final id) is a 400 JSON error.
308	func emptyIDGuard(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
309		return http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
310			p := r.URL.Path
311	
312			documentSegmentEmpty := strings.HasPrefix(p, "/v1/documents//")
313			newFamilySegmentEmpty := false
314			if strings.HasPrefix(p, "/v1/devices/") || strings.HasPrefix(p, "/v1/sessions/") {
315				newFamilySegmentEmpty = strings.Contains(p, "//") || strings.HasSuffix(p, "/")
316			}
317	
318			if documentSegmentEmpty || newFamilySegmentEmpty || malformedNewDocumentPath(p) || malformedSubscribePath(p) || malformedSessionCRDTPath(p) || malformedCRDTPath(p) || malformedSnapshotPath(p) {
319				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "path identifiers must be non-empty strings")
320				return
321			}
322			next.ServeHTTP(w, r)
323		})
324	}

326	// malformedNewDocumentPath reports whether p targets one of the new
327	// long-poll/replay endpoints but is not that endpoint's exact location: a
328	// missing/empty segment, a trailing slash, extra segments, or a "poll"/"replay"
329	// segment in a position short of the registered shape. ServeMux would answer
330	// those with a 301 redirect or a plain-text 404/405; the new endpoints promise
331	// a JSON error and never a redirect, so every such path is a malformed 400.
332	//
333	// Keywords are matched only past the documentID position, so documents that
334	// happen to be named "poll" or "replay" keep their ordinary merge/snapshot/
335	// changes routes.
336	func malformedNewDocumentPath(p string) bool {
337		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/documents/")
338		if !ok {
339			return false
340		}
341		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
342	
343		// Poll endpoint: "poll" must be exactly the third segment, after a
344		// non-empty documentID and "changes".
345		for i, seg := range segs {
346			if seg == "poll" && i > 0 {
347				return !(len(segs) == 3 && segs[0] != "" && segs[1] == "changes")
348			}
349		}
350		// Replay endpoint: "replay" must be exactly the second segment, after a
351		// non-empty documentID.
352		for i, seg := range segs {
353			if seg == "replay" && i > 0 {
354				return !(len(segs) == 2 && segs[0] != "")
355			}
356		}
357		return false
358	}

360	// malformedSubscribePath reports whether p targets the WebSocket subscription
361	// endpoint but is not at its exact location
362	// (/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/changes/subscribe): a
363	// missing "documents"/"changes" segment, an extra segment, or a "subscribe"
364	// segment short of the registered shape. ServeMux would answer those with a
365	// plain-text 404/405; every failure of this endpoint must be a JSON 400
366	// instead. Empty segments are already rejected by the guard itself.
367	//
368	// "subscribe" is treated as the endpoint keyword only in the endpoint's
369	// terminal segment position (the fifth segment, index 4); a session or
370	// document identifier literally named "subscribe" occupies an identifier
371	// position (index 0 or 2) and is therefore left to the ordinary
372	// changes/subscribe routes like any other id.
373	func malformedSubscribePath(p string) bool {
374		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/sessions/")
375		if !ok {
376			return false
377		}
378		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
379		// The CRDT namespace ("crdt" immediately past the document identifier)
380		// has its own guard; "subscribe" there is not the changes-subscribe
381		// keyword.
382		if len(segs) >= 4 && segs[1] == "documents" && segs[3] == "crdt" {
383			return false
384		}
385		for i, seg := range segs {
386			if seg != "subscribe" {
387				continue
388			}
389			// Identifier positions: sessionId (0) and documentId (2). A value of
390			// "subscribe" there is an ordinary identifier, not the endpoint word.
391			if i == 0 || i == 2 {
392				continue
393			}
394			// Endpoint keyword position: the fifth segment must be exactly
395			// "subscribe" with the documents/changes scaffolding around it, and no
396			// segment may follow. Any other occurrence is a malformed path.
397			if i == 4 && len(segs) == 5 &&
398				segs[0] != "" &&
399				segs[1] == "documents" &&
400				segs[2] != "" &&
401				segs[3] == "changes" {
402				return false
403			}
404			return true
405		}
406		return false
407	}

409	// malformedSessionCRDTPath reports whether p targets the session-scoped CRDT
410	// namespace but is not at one of its two exact locations:
411	//
412	//	GET /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/state
413	//	GET /v1/sessions/{sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/state/subscribe
414	//
415	// a missing "state"/"subscribe" segment, an extra segment, or a "crdt" segment
416	// in the keyword position (immediately past the document identifier) short of
417	// one of the registered shapes. ServeMux would answer those with a
418	// plain-text 404/405; every failure of these endpoints must be a JSON 400
419	// instead. Empty segments are already rejected by the guard itself.
420	//
421	// "crdt" is treated as the endpoint keyword only in the fourth segment (index
422	// 3, right after the document identifier); a session or document identifier
423	// literally named "crdt" occupies an identifier position (index 0 or 2) and
424	// keeps its ordinary routes.
425	func malformedSessionCRDTPath(p string) bool {
426		rest, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "/v1/sessions/")
427		if !ok {
428			return false
429		}
430		segs := strings.Split(rest, "/")
431		if len(segs) < 4 || segs[1] != "documents" || segs[3] != "crdt" {
432			return false
433		}
434		// Keyword position reached. The state read is exactly
435		// {sessionId}/documents/{documentId}/crdt/state; the subscription adds
436		// one trailing "subscribe" segment.
437		validState := len(segs) == 5 &&
438			segs[0] != "" &&
439			segs[2] != "" &&
440			segs[4] == "state"
441		validSubscribe := len(segs) == 6 &&
442			segs[0] != "" &&
443			segs[2] != "" &&
444			segs[4] == "state" &&
445			segs[5] == "subscribe"
446		return !(validState || validSubscribe)
447	}

459	// decodeJSONBody enforces the strict POST contract shared by every JSON
460	// endpoint: Content-Type must be application/json, the body is capped at
461	// maxBatchBytes, it must contain exactly one JSON value, and no trailing data
462	// may follow it. Any violation writes a 400 JSON error and returns false; the
463	// caller returns immediately, so no handler reaches the store with malformed
464	// input and rejected requests write nothing.
465	func decodeJSONBody(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request, dst any) bool {
466		mediaType, _, err := mime.ParseMediaType(r.Header.Get("Content-Type"))
467		if err != nil || mediaType != "application/json" {
468			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "Content-Type must be application/json")
469			return false
470		}
471	
472		r.Body = http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, maxBatchBytes)
473		dec := json.NewDecoder(r.Body)
474		if err := dec.Decode(dst); err != nil {
475			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body: "+err.Error())
476			return false
477		}
478		// Reject trailing data after the JSON value.
479		if err := dec.Decode(&struct{}{}); !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
480			writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "invalid JSON body: unexpected trailing content")
481			return false
482		}
483		return true
484	}

863	// parseCursorPath reports whether raw is a decimal non-negative integer and
864	// returns its value. Signs, fractions and other adornments are rejected.
865	func parseCursorPath(raw string) (int64, bool) {
866		if raw == "" {
867			return 0, false
868		}
869		for _, c := range raw {
870			if c < '0' || c > '9' {
871				return 0, false
872			}
873		}
874		n, err := strconv.ParseInt(raw, 10, 64)
875		if err != nil {
876			return 0, false
877		}
878		return n, true
879	}

881	// parseNonNegativeInt reports whether raw is a JSON integer >= 0. Floats,// strings, booleans, null and negative numbers are rejected.
882	func parseNonNegativeInt(raw json.RawMessage) (int64, bool) {
883		var n int64
884		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &n); err != nil || n < 0 {
885			return 0, false
886		}
887		// Guard against values like 1.0 that Unmarshal into int64 on some inputs;
888		// require the literal to contain no fraction or exponent.
889		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(string(raw))
890		if trimmed == "" || trimmed[0] == '-' {
891			return 0, false
892		}
893		for _, c := range trimmed {
894			if c < '0' || c > '9' {
895				return 0, false
896			}
897		}
898		return n, true
899	}
900	
901	// parsePositiveInt reports whether raw is a JSON integer >= 1. Zero, floats,
902	// strings, booleans, null and negative numbers are rejected.
903	func parsePositiveInt(raw json.RawMessage) (int64, bool) {
904		n, ok := parseNonNegativeInt(raw)
905		if !ok || n < 1 {
906			return 0, false
907		}
908		return n, true
909	}

912	// array or a scalar).
913	func isJSONObject(raw json.RawMessage) bool {
914		var m map[string]json.RawMessage
915		if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &m); err != nil || m == nil {
916			return false
917		}
918		return true
919	}

995			if err != nil || v < 0 {

997				return 0, 0, false
998			}
999			after = v
1000		}
1001	
1002		limit = defaultListLimit
1003		if raw := q.Get("limit"); raw != "" {
1004			v, err := strconv.ParseInt(raw, 10, 64)
1005			if err != nil || v < 1 || v > maxListLimit {
1006				writeError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "limit must be an integer between 1 and 1000")
1007				return 0, 0, false
1008			}
1009			limit = v
1010		}
1011	
1012		return after, limit, true
1013	}

1033	// handlePollChanges is the long-polling entry over the change log.

1035	// Query params share the existing change-read constraints: after is a
1036	// non-negative cursor (default 0) and limit is 1..1000 (default 100); waitMs
1037	// is 0..30000 (default 0). Rows already past after return immediately; a known
1038	// document caught up to after parks until the first new commit or the wait

1041	// expiry echoes the caller's cursor and never advances it. A client
1042	// disconnect simply stops the wait and writes nothing.

1047		if !ok {
